test_1996|t|
test_1996|a|In the framework of toxicology , a testing strategy can be viewed as a series of steps which are taken to come to a final prediction about a characteristic of a compound under study .

test_1997|t|
test_1997|a|The testing strategy is performed as a single - step procedure , usually called a test battery , using simultaneously all information collected on different endpoints , or as tiered approach in which a decision tree is followed .

test_1998|t|
test_1998|a|Design of a testing strategy involves statistical considerations , such as the development of a statistical prediction model .

test_1999|t|

test_2000|t|

test_2001|t|
test_2001|a|However , without thorough statistical evaluations a testing strategy cannot be identified .

test_5153|a|MetalPDB : a database of metal sites in biological macromolecular structures .

test_5154|t|
test_5154|a|We present here MetalPDB ( freely accessible at http : / / metalweb . cerm . unifi . it ) , a novel resource aimed at conveying the information available on the three - dimensional ( 3D ) structures of metal - binding biological macromolecules in a consistent and effective manner .

test_5155|t|
test_5155|a|This is achieved through the systematic and automated representation of metal - binding sites in proteins and nucleic acids by way of Minimal Functional Sites ( MFSs ) .

test_5156|t|
test_5156|a|MFSs are 3D templates that describe the local environment around the metal ( s ) independently of the larger context of the macromolecular structure embedding the site ( s ) , and are the central objects of MetalPDB design .

test_5157|t|
test_5157|a|MFSs are grouped into equistructural ( broadly defined as sites found in corresponding positions in similar structures ) and equivalent sites ( equistructural sites that contain the same metals ) , allowing users to easily analyse similarities and variations in metal - macromolecule interactions , and to link them to functional information .

test_5158|t|
test_5158|a|The web interface of MetalPDB allows access to a comprehensive overview of metal - containing biological structures , providing a basis to investigate the basic principles governing the properties of these systems .

test_5159|t|
test_5159|a|MetalPDB is updated monthly in an automated manner .

test_5653|a|Insight into tissue unbound concentration : utility in drug discovery and development .

test_5654|t|
test_5654|a|In a preclinical setting , plasma or whole tissue drug concentrations are often correlated with pharmacodynamics , although according to the free drug hypothesis , unbound drug concentration should be more pharmacologically relevant .

test_5655|t|
test_5655|a|Alternatively , blood concentrations may be a good surrogate for tissue concentration for passively permeable compounds .

test_5656|t|
test_5656|a|However , for a large number of compounds that are substrates for uptake and / or efflux transporters expressed at the tissue level , significant discrepancies are expected between unbound concentrations in blood and those in tissues .

test_5657|t|
test_5657|a|Consequently , attempts have been made to measure tissue unbound drug concentrations using tissue homogenates , slices and microdialysis .

test_5658|t|
test_5658|a|Mathematical expressions for calculating the rate and extent of drug distribution into tissues have also been established .

test_5659|t|

test_6147|t|
test_6147|a|PTMcode : a database of known and predicted functional associations between post - translational modifications in proteins .

test_6148|t|
test_6148|a|Post - translational modifications ( PTMs ) are involved in the regulation and structural stabilization of eukaryotic proteins .

test_6149|t|
test_6149|a|The combination of individual PTM states is a key to modulate cellular functions as became evident in a few well - studied proteins .

test_6150|t|
test_6150|a|This combinatorial setting , dubbed the PTM code , has been proposed to be extended to whole proteomes in eukaryotes .

test_6151|t|
test_6151|a|Although we are still far from deciphering such a complex language , thousands of protein PTM sites are being mapped by high - throughput technologies , thus providing sufficient data for comparative analysis .

test_6152|t|
test_6152|a|PTMcode ( http : / / ptmcode . embl . de ) aims to compile known and predicted PTM associations to provide a framework that would enable hypothesis - driven experimental or computational analysis of various scales .

test_6153|t|
test_6153|a|In its first release , PTMcode provides PTM functional associations of 13 different PTM types within proteins in 8 eukaryotes .

test_6154|t|
test_6154|a|They are based on five evidence channels : a literature survey , residue co - evolution , structural proximity , PTMs at the same residue and location within PTM highly enriched protein regions ( hotspots ) .

test_6155|t|
test_6155|a|PTMcode is presented as a protein - based searchable database with an interactive web interface providing the context of the co - regulation of nearly 75 000 residues in > 10 000 proteins .

test_7592|a|Phase transition - induced elasticity of alpha - helical bioelastomeric fibres and networks .

test_7593|t|
test_7593|a|Natural elastomeric fibres play central structural and functional roles in a variety of tissues produced by many organisms from diverse Phyla .

test_7594|t|
test_7594|a|Most of these fibres feature amorphous structure and their long - range elastic response is well described within the framework of entropic ( rubber - like ) elasticity .

test_7595|t|
test_7595|a|Recently , it has been recognized that long - range reversible deformation can also occur in biomacromolecular fibres or networks that feature significant secondary structure and long - range order .

test_7596|t|
test_7596|a|Their elastomeric response is then associated with conformational changes of the backbone of the constitutive protein - based polymers .

test_7597|t|
test_7597|a|Under axially imposed loads , several groups of proteins whose structure is dominated by alpha - helical coiled - coil structures can undergo unfolding transitions and secondary structure transformations , for example from coiled - coil alpha - helices to beta - sheet strands .

test_7598|t|
test_7598|a|In contrast to rubber - like biopolymers , the retractive elastic force in these biomacromolecular materials is not dominated by a return to a maximum entropic state , but is mostly the result of variations in internal energy associated with the conformational changes .

test_7599|t|
test_7599|a|Here , a review of alpha - helix based elastomeric materials is presented that encompasses examples and experimental evidence across multiple length scales , from the molecular to the macroscopic scale .
test_7599	20	33	alpha - helix	chemical	MESH:C053936

test_8616|t|
test_8616|a|Qalibra : a general model for food risk - benefit assessment that quantifies variability and uncertainty .

test_8617|t|
test_8617|a|The EU project BRAFO proposed a framework for risk - benefit assessment of foods , or changes in diet , that present both potential risks and potential benefits to consumers ( Hoekstra et al . , 2012a ) .

test_8618|t|
test_8618|a|In higher tiers of the BRAFO framework , risks and benefits are integrated quantitatively to estimate net health impact measured in DALYs or QALYs ( disability - or quality - adjusted life years ) .

test_8619|t|
test_8619|a|This paper describes a general model that was developed by a second EU project , Qalibra , to assist users in conducting these assessments .

test_8620|t|
test_8620|a|Its flexible design makes it applicable to a wide range of dietary questions involving different nutrients , contaminants and health effects .

test_8621|t|
test_8621|a|Account can be taken of variation between consumers in their diets and also other characteristics relevant to the estimation of risk and benefit , such as body weight , gender and age .

test_8622|t|
test_8622|a|Uncertainty in any input parameter may be quantified probabilistically , using probability distributions , or deterministically by repeating the assessment with alternative assumptions .

test_8623|t|
test_8623|a|Uncertainties that are not quantified should be evaluated qualitatively .

test_8624|t|
test_8624|a|Outputs produced by the model are illustrated using results from a simple assessment of fish consumption .

test_9772|t|
test_9772|a|Perspectives on the reaction force constant .

test_9773|t|
test_9773|a|A synchronous , concerted chemical process is rigorously divided by the reaction force F ( R ) , the negative gradient of V ( R ) , into " reactant " and " product " regions which are dominated by structural changes and an intervening " transition " region which is electronically intensive .

test_9774|t|
test_9774|a|The reaction force constant kappa ( R ) , the second derivative of V ( R ) , is negative throughout the transition region , not just at the nominal transition state , at which kappa ( R ) has a minimum .

test_9775|t|
test_9775|a|This is consistent with experimental evidence that there is a transition region , not simply a specific point .

test_9776|t|
test_9776|a|We show graphically that significant nonsynchronicity in the process is associated with the development of a maximum of kappa ( R ) in the transition region , which increases as the process becomes more nonsynchronous .

test_9777|t|
test_9777|a|( We speculate that for a nonconcerted process this maximum is actually positive . ) Thus , kappa ( R ) can serve as an indicator of the level of nonsynchronicity .

test_9790|a|Calculation of wave - functions with frozen orbitals in mixed quantum mechanics / molecular mechanics methods .

test_9791|t|
test_9791|a|II .

test_9792|t|
test_9792|a|Application of the local basis equation .

test_9793|t|
test_9793|a|The application of the local basis equation ( Ferenczy and Adams , J . Chem . Phys . 2009 , 130 , 134108 ) in mixed quantum mechanics / molecular mechanics ( QM / MM ) and quantum mechanics / quantum mechanics ( QM / QM ) methods is investigated .

test_9794|t|
test_9794|a|This equation is suitable to derive local basis nonorthogonal orbitals that minimize the energy of the system and it exhibits good convergence properties in a self - consistent field solution .

test_9795|t|
test_9795|a|These features make the equation appropriate to be used in mixed QM / MM and QM / QM methods to optimize orbitals in the field of frozen localized orbitals connecting the subsystems .

test_9796|t|
test_9796|a|Calculations performed for several properties in divers systems show that the method is robust with various choices of the frozen orbitals and frontier atom properties .

test_9797|t|
test_9797|a|With appropriate basis set assignment , it gives results equivalent with those of a related approach [ G . G . Ferenczy previous paper in this issue ] using the Huzinaga equation .

test_9798|t|
test_9798|a|Thus , the local basis equation can be used in mixed QM / MM methods with small size quantum subsystems to calculate properties in good agreement with reference Hartree - Fock - Roothaan results .

test_9799|t|
test_9799|a|It is shown that bond charges are not necessary when the local basis equation is applied , although they are required for the self - consistent field solution of the Huzinaga equation based method .

test_9800|t|
test_9800|a|Conversely , the deformation of the wave - function near to the boundary is observed without bond charges and this has a significant effect on deprotonation energies but a less pronounced effect when the total charge of the system is conserved .

test_9801|t|
test_9801|a|The local basis equation can also be used to define a two layer quantum system with nonorthogonal localized orbitals surrounding the central delocalized quantum subsystem .

test_14118|a|Dose finding by concentration - response versus dose - response : a simulation - based comparison .

test_14119|t|
test_14119|a|AIM : The investigations reported here aimed to evaluate the incremental benefit for dose finding by concentration - response analysis versus dose - response analysis .

test_14120|t|
test_14120|a|METHODS : Trials were simulated using an Emax model for a range of scenarios of drug properties , trial design options and target response levels .

test_14121|t|
test_14121|a|The simulated data were analysed by concentration - response and dose - response modelling ; a dose was then chosen to target a specific response level in a confirmatory trial .

test_14122|t|
test_14122|a|The two approaches were compared in terms of the quality of model parameter estimation and the success rate for the confirmatory trial .

test_14123|t|
test_14123|a|RESULTS : While the accuracy for ED50 estimation was comparably good with both approaches , the precision was up to 90 % higher with concentration - response approach .

test_14124|t|
test_14124|a|The difference was most notable when clearance was highly variable between subjects and the top dose was relatively low .

test_14125|t|
test_14125|a|The higher precision by the concentration - response analysis lead to better dose selection and up to 20 % higher success rate for the subsequent confirmatory trial .

test_14126|t|
test_14126|a|The relatively small difference in success rate translated into a remarkable difference in sample size requirement .

test_14127|t|
test_14127|a|CONCLUSION : By customising these parameters , the approach and the findings can be applied to assessing the value of pharmacokinetic sampling in particular trial situations .

test_14669|t|
test_14669|a|Temperature - dependent vapor pressures of solid explosives and their byproducts are calculated to an accuracy of 0 . 32 log units using a modified form of the conductor - like screening model for real solvents ( COSMO - RS ) .

test_14670|t|
test_14670|a|Accurate predictions for solids within COSMO - RS require correction for the free energy of fusion as well as other effects such as van der Waals interactions .

test_14671|t|

test_15964|a|Application of the compensated Arrhenius formalism to fluidity data of polar organic liquids .

test_15965|t|
test_15965|a|The temperature dependence of viscosity ( the reciprocal of fluidity ) in polar liquids has been studied for over a century , but the available theoretical models have serious limitations .

test_15966|t|

test_18037|a|Considering the impact drug - like properties have on the chance of success .

test_18038|t|
test_18038|a|Many definitions of ' drug - like ' compound properties have been published ; based on the analysis of simple molecular properties of successful drugs .

test_18039|t|
test_18039|a|These are typically presented as rules that define acceptable boundaries for these properties .

test_18040|t|

test_18041|t|

test_18042|t|
test_18042|a|Alternatively , compounds can be ranked according to their similarity to marketed drugs using a continuous measure of drug - likeness .

test_18043|t|

test_18770|t|
test_18770|a|Lyotropic phases of amphiphiles are a prototypical example of self - assemblies .

test_18771|t|

test_18772|t|
test_18772|a|In this paper , we demonstrate a new paradigm for membrane shape control where the electrostatic coupling of charged membranes to short DNA ( sDNA ) , with tunable temperature - dependent end - to - end stacking interactions , enables switching between the inverted gyroid cubic structure ( QII ( G ) ) and the inverted hexagonal phase ( HII ( C ) ) .

test_18773|t|

test_18774|t|

test_20129|a|Constraint Network Analysis ( CNA ) : A Python Software Package for Efficiently Linking Biomacromolecular Structure , Flexibility , ( Thermo - ) Stability , and Function .

test_20130|t|
test_20130|a|For deriving maximal advantage from information on biomacromolecular flexibility and rigidity , results from rigidity analyses must be linked to biologically relevant characteristics of a structure .

test_20131|t|
test_20131|a|Here , we describe the Python - based software package Constraint Network Analysis ( CNA ) developed for this task .

test_20132|t|
test_20132|a|CNA functions as a front - and backend to the graph - based rigidity analysis software FIRST .

test_20133|t|
test_20133|a|CNA goes beyond the mere identification of flexible and rigid regions in a biomacromolecule in that it ( I ) provides a refined modeling of thermal unfolding simulations that also considers the temperature - dependence of hydrophobic tethers , ( II ) allows performing rigidity analyses on ensembles of network topologies , either generated from structural ensembles or by using the concept of fuzzy noncovalent constraints , and ( III ) computes a set of global and local indices for quantifying biomacromolecular stability .

test_20134|t|
test_20134|a|This leads to more robust results from rigidity analyses and extends the application domain of rigidity analyses in that phase transition points ( " melting points " ) and unfolding nuclei ( " structural weak spots " ) are determined automatically .

test_20135|t|
test_20135|a|Furthermore , CNA robustly handles small - molecule ligands in general .

test_20136|t|
test_20136|a|Such advancements are important for applying rigidity analysis to data - driven protein engineering and for estimating the influence of ligand molecules on biomacromolecular stability .

test_20137|t|
test_20137|a|CNA maintains the efficiency of FIRST such that the analysis of a single protein structure takes a few seconds for systems of several hundred residues on a single core .

test_20138|t|
test_20138|a|These features make CNA an interesting tool for linking biomacromolecular structure , flexibility , ( thermo - ) stability , and function .

test_20139|t|
test_20139|a|CNA is available from http : / / cpclab . uni - duesseldorf . de / software for nonprofit organizations .

test_20373|t|
test_20373|a|Time - split cross - validation as a method for estimating the goodness of prospective prediction .

test_20374|t|
test_20374|a|Cross - validation is a common method to validate a QSAR model .

test_20375|t|
test_20375|a|In cross - validation , some compounds are held out as a test set , while the remaining compounds form a training set .

test_20376|t|
test_20376|a|A model is built from the training set , and the test set compounds are predicted on that model .

test_20377|t|
test_20377|a|The agreement of the predicted and observed activity values of the test set ( measured by , say , R ( 2 ) ) is an estimate of the self - consistency of the model and is sometimes taken as an indication of the predictivity of the model .

test_20378|t|
test_20378|a|This estimate of predictivity can be optimistic or pessimistic compared to true prospective prediction , depending how compounds in the test set are selected .

test_20379|t|
test_20379|a|Here , we show that time - split selection gives an R ( 2 ) that is more like that of true prospective prediction than the R ( 2 ) from random selection ( too optimistic ) or from our analog of leave - class - out selection ( too pessimistic ) .

test_20380|t|
test_20380|a|Time - split selection should be used in addition to random selection as a standard for cross - validation in QSAR model building .

test_21085|a|Force nanoscopy of cell mechanics and cell adhesion .

test_21086|t|
test_21086|a|Cells are constantly exposed to mechanical stimuli in their environment and have several evolved mechanisms to sense and respond to these cues .

test_21087|t|
test_21087|a|It is becoming increasingly recognized that many cell types , from bacteria to mammalian cells , possess a diverse set of proteins to translate mechanical cues into biochemical signalling and to mediate cell surface interactions such as cell adhesion .

test_21088|t|
test_21088|a|Moreover , the mechanical properties of cells are involved in regulating cell function as well as serving as indicators of disease states .

test_21089|t|
test_21089|a|Importantly , the recent development of biophysical tools and nanoscale methods has facilitated a deeper understanding of the role that physical forces play in modulating cell mechanics and cell adhesion .

test_21090|t|
test_21090|a|Here , we discuss how atomic force microscopy ( AFM ) has recently been used to investigate cell mechanics and cell adhesion at the single - cell and single - molecule levels .

test_21091|t|
test_21091|a|This knowledge is critical to our understanding of the molecular mechanisms that govern mechanosensing , mechanotransduction , and mechanoresponse in living cells .

test_21092|t|
test_21092|a|While pushing living cells with the AFM tip provides a means to quantify their mechanical properties and examine their response to nanoscale forces , pulling single surface proteins with a functionalized tip allows one to understand their role in sensing and adhesion .

test_21093|t|
test_21093|a|The combination of these nanoscale techniques with modern molecular biology approaches , genetic engineering and optical microscopies provides a powerful platform for understanding the sophisticated functions of the cell surface machinery , and its role in the onset and progression of complex diseases .

test_21171|t|
test_21171|a|They are utilized in order to overcome the major challenges being associated with this route of administration - namely poor solubility ( I ) , poor permeability ( II ) and poor GI - stability ( III ) .

test_21172|t|
test_21172|a|In order to improve drug solubility nanonization of the API , the use of solid lipid nanoparticles and porous adsorbent particles have shown great potential .

test_21173|t|
test_21173|a|Nanocrystals and selfnanoemulsifying drug delivery systems ( SNEDDS ) resulted already in numerous marketed drug products .

test_21174|t|
test_21174|a|Moreover , proof - of - principle studies for nanocarrier systems providing enhanced oral drug uptake are available .

test_21175|t|
test_21175|a|By providing a comparatively more intimate contact with the absorption membrane , a prolonged GI - residence time and / or exhibiting permeation enhancing properties , oral absorption can be strongly improved .

test_21176|t|
test_21176|a|Likely because of safety considerations and because of insufficiently high bioavailability improvements ( < 5 - fold ) , however , a commercial interest in these systems is limited .

test_21177|t|
test_21177|a|Poor GI - stability can be overcome by incorporating the drug in nanocarrier systems providing a protective effect towards an enzymatic attack in the GI - tract .

test_21178|t|
test_21178|a|Furthermore , as nanocarrier systems can at least to some extent diffuse into the mucus gel layer releasing their payload there , a presystemic metabolism of the drug on the way between the delivery system and the absorption membrane can be excluded .

test_21179|t|
test_21179|a|Future trends are mainly focusing on carrier systems capable of not just improving solubility but providing also controlled drug release as well as on nanocarrier systems capable of efficiently permeating the mucus gel layer without destroying it .

test_21491|t|
test_21491|a|A GLUE uncertainty analysis of a drying model of pharmaceutical granules .

test_21492|t|
test_21492|a|A shift from batch processing towards continuous processing is of interest in the pharmaceutical industry .

test_21493|t|
test_21493|a|However , this transition requires detailed knowledge and process understanding of all consecutive unit operations in a continuous manufacturing line to design adequate control strategies .

test_21494|t|
test_21494|a|This can be facilitated by developing mechanistic models of the multi - phase systems in the process .

test_21495|t|
test_21495|a|Since modelling efforts only started recently in this field , uncertainties about the model predictions are generally neglected .

test_21496|t|
test_21496|a|However , model predictions have an inherent uncertainty ( i . e . prediction uncertainty ) originating from uncertainty in input data , model parameters , model structure , boundary conditions and software .

test_21497|t|
test_21497|a|In this paper , the model prediction uncertainty is evaluated for a model describing the continuous drying of single pharmaceutical wet granules in a six - segmented fluidized bed drying unit , which is part of the full continuous from - powder - to - tablet manufacturing line ( Consigma ( TM ) , GEA Pharma Systems ) .

test_21498|t|
test_21498|a|A validated model describing the drying behaviour of a single pharmaceutical granule in two consecutive phases is used .

test_21499|t|
test_21499|a|First of all , the effect of the assumptions at the particle level on the prediction uncertainty is assessed .

test_21500|t|
test_21500|a|Secondly , the paper focuses on the influence of the most sensitive parameters in the model .

test_21501|t|
test_21501|a|Finally , a combined analysis ( particle level plus most sensitive parameters ) is performed and discussed .

test_21502|t|
test_21502|a|To propagate the uncertainty originating from the parameter uncertainty to the model output , the Generalized Likelihood Uncertainty Estimation ( GLUE ) method is used .

test_21503|t|
test_21503|a|This method enables a modeller to incorporate the information obtained from the experimental data in the assessment of the uncertain model predictions and to find a balance between model performance and data precision .

test_21504|t|
test_21504|a|A detailed evaluation of the obtained uncertainty analysis results is made with respect to the model structure , interactions between parameters and uncertainty boundaries .

test_23783|a|RNA global alignment in the joint sequence - structure space using elastic shape analysis .

test_23784|t|
test_23784|a|The functions of RNAs , like proteins , are determined by their structures , which , in turn , are determined by their sequences .

test_23785|t|
test_23785|a|Comparison / alignment of RNA molecules provides an effective means to predict their functions and understand their evolutionary relationships .

test_23786|t|
test_23786|a|For RNA sequence alignment , most methods developed for protein and DNA sequence alignment can be directly applied .

test_23787|t|
test_23787|a|RNA 3 - dimensional structure alignment , on the other hand , tends to be more difficult than protein structure alignment due to the lack of regular secondary structures as observed in proteins .

test_23788|t|
test_23788|a|Most of the existing RNA 3D structure alignment methods use only the backbone geometry and ignore the sequence information .

test_23789|t|
test_23789|a|Using both the sequence and backbone geometry information in RNA alignment may not only produce more accurate classification , but also deepen our understanding of the sequence - structure - function relationship of RNA molecules .

test_23790|t|
test_23790|a|In this study , we developed a new RNA alignment method based on elastic shape analysis ( ESA ) .

test_23791|t|

test_23792|t|
test_23792|a|The similarity between two RNA molecules is quantified by a formal distance , geodesic distance .

test_23793|t|

test_24182|a|Macromolecular amplification of binding response in superaptamer hydrogels .

test_24183|t|
test_24183|a|It is becoming more important to detect ultralow concentrations of analytes for biomedical , environmental , and national security applications .

test_24184|t|
test_24184|a|Equally important is that new methods should be easy to use , inexpensive , portable , and if possible allow detection by the naked eye .

test_24185|t|
test_24185|a|By and large , detection of low concentrations of analytes cannot be achieved directly but requires signal amplification by catalysts , macromolecules , metal surfaces , or supramolecular aggregates .

test_24186|t|
test_24186|a|The rapidly progressing field of macromolecular signal amplification has been advanced using conjugated polymers , chirality in polymers , solvating polymers , and polymerization / depolymerization strategies .

test_24187|t|
test_24187|a|A new type of aptamer - based hydrogel with specific response to target proteins presented in this report demonstrates an additional category of macromolecular signal amplification .

test_24188|t|
test_24188|a|This superaptamer assembly provides the first example of using protein - specific aptamers to create volume - changing hydrogels with amplified response to the target protein .

test_24189|t|
test_24189|a|A remarkable aspect of these superaptamer hydrogels is that volume shrinking is visible to the naked eye down to femtomolar concentrations of protein .

test_24190|t|
test_24190|a|This extraordinary macromolecular amplification is attributed to a complex interplay between protein - aptamer supramolecular cross - links and the consequential reduction of excluded volume in the hydrogel .

test_24191|t|
test_24191|a|Specific recognition is even maintained in biological matrices such as urine and tears .

test_24192|t|
test_24192|a|Furthermore , the gels can be dried for long - term storage and regenerated for use without loss of activity .

test_24193|t|
test_24193|a|In practice , the ease of this biomarker detection method offers an alternative to traditional analytical techniques that require sophisticated instrumentation and highly trained personnel .

test_24582|a|Empirical evidence demonstrates that the Druckrey - K u pfm u ller toxicity model , which was validated for chemical carcinogens in the early 1960s , is also applicable to a wide range of toxic compounds in ecotoxicology .

test_24583|t|
test_24583|a|According to this model , the character of a poison is primarily determined by the reversibility of critical receptor binding .

test_24584|t|

test_26259|a|Simulations of droplet coalescence in simple shear flow .

test_26261|t|
test_26261|a|In general , liquid droplets colliding in a liquid medium coalesce when the capillary number is less than a critical value .

test_26262|t|
test_26262|a|We present simulations of droplet collisions and coalescence in simple shear flow using the free - energy binary - liquid lattice Boltzmann method .

test_26263|t|
test_26263|a|In previous simulations of low - speed collisions , droplets coalesced at unrealistically high capillary numbers .

test_26264|t|
test_26264|a|Simulations of non - coalescing droplets have not been reported , and therefore the critical capillary number for simulated collisions was unknown .

test_26265|t|
test_26265|a|By simulating droplets with radii up to 100 lattice nodes , we determine the critical capillary number for coalescence and quantify the effects of several numerical and geometric parameters .

test_26266|t|
test_26266|a|The simulations were performed with a well - resolved interface , a Reynolds number of one , and capillary numbers from 0 . 01 to 0 . 2 .

test_26267|t|
test_26267|a|The ratio of the droplet radius and interface thickness has the greatest effect on the critical capillary number .

test_26268|t|
test_26268|a|As in experiments , the critical capillary number decreases with increasing droplet size .

test_26269|t|
test_26269|a|A second numerical parameter , the interface diffusivity ( Peclet number ) also influences the conditions for coalescence : coalescence occurs at higher capillary numbers with lower Peclet numbers ( higher diffusivity ) .

test_26270|t|
test_26270|a|The effects of the vertical offset between the droplets and the confinement of the droplets were also studied .

test_26271|t|
test_26271|a|Physically reasonable results were obtained and provide insight into the conditions for coalescence .

test_26272|a|Simulations that match the conditions of experiments reported in the literature remain computationally impractical .
